paragraph: Every day, about twenty million barrels of oil pass through a channel barely thirty-nine kilometres wide. On one side, Iran. On the other, Oman and the Emirates. If this strait closed for even a week, petrol prices on the other side of the planet would jump overnight. So why has nobody ever managed to shut it? The answer is stranger than you think.
note: wer_norm treats kilometers/kilometres and digits as equal
